result:
The proposed answer, q^{2D(r−1)}, is most likely wrong. The correct ratio is probably q^{D(r−1)}, though I am reasoning from memory and have not confirmed this against Hattori's paper. The proposed solution itself admits it is guessing: it tries q^{(r−1)D}, then q^{2(r−1)D}, and settles on the latter without justification.

**Heuristic check.** Work on the ordinary locus, where the ℘-torsion of the Drinfeld module has an étale part and a multiplicative part.

1. A Γ₁(℘^r)-structure is a point of exact order ℘^r. On the ordinary locus these points lie in the étale part, which is isomorphic to A/℘^r.
2. Passing from Γ₁(℘) to Γ₁(℘^r) therefore gives a cover of degree q^{D(r−1)}. This is the p-part of (A/℘^r)^×, which has order q^{D(r−1)}.
3. The classical analogue is that the finite-slope part at level Γ₁(p^r) carries p^{r−1} characters of the p-part of (ℤ/p^r)^×, each with multiplicity 1.
4. In characteristic p these characters all collapse to the trivial one. The count p^{r−1} then survives as a generalized-eigenspace multiplicity, here q^{D(r−1)}.
5. Nothing in this picture supplies an extra factor of q^{D(r−1)} from a unipotent part. The proposed exponent 2D(r−1) rests only on a loose coset count that the solution does not justify.

So the ratio should be q^{D(r−1)}, not q^{2D(r−1)}.

VERDICT: REJECT
